newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car sales seen strong ahead of tax move.
newsitem.headline: Japan car sales seen strong ahead of tax move.

text.p: Japan's domestic vehicle sales are likely to continue to surge this month as customers rush to buy new cars before a rise in Japan's national sales tax in April, car industry officials said on Monday.

"Domestic (car) sales are likely to post double-digit growth in March. Car dealers will be trying to achieve better sales results in March, the last month of their fiscal year," said an official at the Japan Automobile Dealers' Association.
"In addition, we can expect consumers to rush to buy new cars this month ahead of the sales tax rise," the industry group official told Reuters.

Earlier, the group announced that domestic vehicle sales in Japan in February rose 11 percent from a year earlier to 511,375 units. It was the fourth straight month in which the sales rise had been in double digits.
Japan's national sales tax rate is due to be raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
All Japanese vehicle makers except Mitsubishi Motors saw their sales rise in February on a year-on-year basis due to buoyant demand ahead of the tax rise, the association official said.
A spokesman for Nissan Motor Co Ltd said: "In view of current strong demand, overall domestic sales are likely to mark a two-digit gain this month."

All big carmakers are expecting March sales to rise on a year-on-year basis ahead of the tax rise, and because of the seasonal sales drive by car dealers to polish up their firms' balance sheets before the end of the financial year on March 31.

Mitsubishi's sales fell 2.6 percent from a year earlier to 42,682 units in February as its Pajero heavy sport-utility vehicle (SUV) was overshadowed by Toyota's Land Cruiser Prado, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.

He added that the "new model effect" -- a surge in demand when a new model is unveiled -- for the Pajero Jr compact SUV had petered out. Toyota's Prado was remodelled in May last year while the last complete overhaul of the Pajero was in January 1991.
